def: A benchmark result measured and published by the model's own developer, usually under settings chosen to suit that model.
A leaderboard built from users voting between two anonymous model answers to their own prompts.
A model in which the chance that one item beats another is a logistic function of the difference in their strengths, fitted to pairwise outcomes.
A regression adjustment for answer length and formatting so that preference ratings reflect substance more than presentation.
The span of positions a model occupies across bootstrap resamples of the votes, showing how firmly its rank is established.
Testing many private variants and publishing only the best result, which inflates the published score without any dishonest measurement.
The upward bias in the best of several noisy measurements, because luck as well as quality put it on top.
The prompts, tools, loop and limits wrapped around a model, which belong to the score of an agent benchmark as much as the model does.
A judge-based win rate corrected, usually by regression, to estimate what it would be if the compared answers had equal length.
The observation that a measure which becomes a target stops being a good measure, as optimisation exploits its gaps.
